**Aubrey Drake Graham** (born October 24, 1986) is a Canadian rapper, singer and actor. He is considered as one of the greatest rappers of all time[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-name-8) and is credited with popularizing [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") sensibilities in [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop"). Drake first gained recognition as [Jimmy Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Brooks "Jimmy Brooks") in the [CTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CTV_Television_Network "CTV Television Network") teen drama series _[Degrassi: The Next Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Degrassi:_The_Next_Generation "Degrassi: The Next Generation")_ (2001–2008) and began his music career by [independently](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unsigned_artist "Unsigned artist") releasing the mixtapes _[Room for Improvement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Room_for_Improvement_\(mixtape\) "Room for Improvement \(mixtape\)")_ (2006), _[Comeback Season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comeback_Season_\(mixtape\) "Comeback Season \(mixtape\)")_ (2007), and _[So Far Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So_Far_Gone_\(mixtape\) "So Far Gone \(mixtape\)")_ (2009), before signing with [Young Money Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Money_Entertainment "Young Money Entertainment").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-9)
Drake's debut album, _[Thank Me Later](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank_Me_Later "Thank Me Later")_ (2010), debuted atop the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") and included his breakthrough hit "[Best I Ever Had](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_I_Ever_Had "Best I Ever Had")". He followed it with the albums _[Take Care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take_Care "Take Care")_ (2011) and _[Nothing Was the Same](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nothing_Was_the_Same "Nothing Was the Same")_ (2013); the former was included on _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ 's "[500 Greatest Albums of All Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone's_500_Greatest_Albums_of_All_Time "Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time")" list. His fourth studio album, _[Views](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Views_\(album\) "Views \(album\)")_ (2016), led the _Billboard_ 200 for 13 weeks. Its second single, "[One Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Dance "One Dance")", became the [first song to surpass 1 billion streams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Spotify_streaming_records "List of Spotify streaming records") on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"). In 2018, Drake released his fifth studio album, _[Scorpion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorpion_\(Drake_album\) "Scorpion \(Drake album\)")_ , spending [29 weeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_weeks_at_number_one_in_a_calendar_year "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") atop the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") with its singles: "[God's Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God's_Plan_\(song\) "God's Plan \(song\)")", "[Nice for What](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nice_for_What "Nice for What")", and "[In My Feelings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Feelings "In My Feelings")". Throughout the 2020s, Drake amassed six US number-one albums, including _[Certified Lover Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Lover_Boy "Certified Lover Boy")_ (2021) and _[Iceman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iceman_\(album\) "Iceman \(album\)")_ (2026), which respectively spawned [nine and ten US top ten songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_top_ten_songs_from_one_album "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones"). In 2026, he became the first artist to occupy the top three spots on the _Billboard_ 200.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-10)
As an entrepreneur, Drake founded the record label [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound"), production company [DreamCrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DreamCrew "DreamCrew"), and the fragrance house Better World. In 2013, he became the "global ambassador" of the [Toronto Raptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Raptors "Toronto Raptors"), joining their executive committee and later obtaining naming rights to their practice facility [OVO Athletic Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Athletic_Centre "OVO Athletic Centre"). In 2016, he began collaborating with [Brent Hocking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brent_Hocking "Brent Hocking") on the [bourbon whiskey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourbon_whiskey "Bourbon whiskey") [Virginia Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Black_Whiskey "Virginia Black Whiskey"). Drake is a co-owner of the gaming organization [100 Thieves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/100_Thieves "100 Thieves"), and heads the OVO fashion label and the Nocta collaboration with [Nike, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nike,_Inc. "Nike, Inc.") His 2015 partnership with [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") has been credited with the successful launch of that platform. Drake has received widespread media coverage due to his extravagant lifestyle and [rap feuds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap_feud "Rap feud"), including [with Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake%E2%80%93Kanye_West_feud "Drake–Kanye West feud") and [with Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake%E2%80%93Kendrick_Lamar_feud "Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud").
Among the world's [best-selling music artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_music_artists "List of best-selling music artists"), with over 170 million units sold, Drake is also ranked as the highest-certified [digital singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-certified_music_artists_in_the_United_States "List of highest-certified music artists in the United States") artist in the United States.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-billboard_riaa2-11) [His accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Drake "List of awards and nominations received by Drake") include 5 [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award"), 6 [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards "American Music Awards"), [41 _Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Award#Most_wins "Billboard Music Award"), 2 [Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Awards "Brit Awards"), and 3 [Juno Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Awards "Juno Awards"). _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard \(magazine\)")_ named him the [Artist of the Decade (2010s)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Decade-End#2010s "Billboard Decade-End"), the [highest-grossing hip-hop touring artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_live_music_artists#Hip-hop "List of highest-grossing live music artists"), and the [fourth greatest pop star of the 21st century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard's_Greatest_Pop_Stars#21st_Century "Billboard's Greatest Pop Stars"). He has achieved [15 _Billboard_ 200 number-one albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200#Most_number-one_albums "Billboard 200") and [14 _Billboard_ Hot 100 number-one singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artists_with_the_most_number-ones_on_the_U.S._Billboard_Hot_100_chart "Artists with the most number-ones on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart");[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Sicko_mode-12) both rank as a record among male solo artists. He additionally has the most number-one singles on the [R&B/Hip-Hop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R&B/Hip-Hop_Airplay "R&B/Hip-Hop Airplay"), [Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs"), [Hot Rap Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Rap_Songs "Hot Rap Songs"), and [Rhythmic Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_Airplay "Rhythmic Airplay") charts.
## Early life
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Forest_Hill_Collegiate_Institute.JPG/250px-Forest_Hill_Collegiate_Institute.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Forest_Hill_Collegiate_Institute.JPG)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e8/Vaughan_road_academy_mon.jpeg/250px-Vaughan_road_academy_mon.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vaughan_road_academy_mon.jpeg)
For high school, Drake attended [Forest Hill Collegiate Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Hill_Collegiate_Institute "Forest Hill Collegiate Institute") (left) and [Vaughan Road Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaughan_Road_Academy "Vaughan Road Academy") (right).
Aubrey Drake Graham[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-allmusic-13) was born on October 24, 1986, in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), Ontario. His father, Dennis Graham, is an [African-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American "African-American") drummer from [Memphis, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis,_Tennessee "Memphis, Tennessee"), who once performed with musician [Jerry Lee Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Lee_Lewis "Jerry Lee Lewis").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-14)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-auto3-15) His mother, Sandra "Sandi" Graham ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") Sher), is a [Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Canada "History of the Jews in Canada") [Ashkenazi Jew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jew "Ashkenazi Jew"), who worked as an English teacher and florist.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:4-16)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-17)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-18)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:5-19)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-20) Graham performed at Club Bluenote in Toronto, where he met Sandra, who was in attendance.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-auto3-15) Drake is a dual citizen of the United States and Canada, the former derived from Graham.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-vibe.com-21)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Tanabe-22)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-23) In his youth, he attended a Jewish day school and became a [bar mitzvah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_mitzvah "Bar mitzvah").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-24)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-mytvn1-25)
Drake's parents divorced when he was five years old. After the divorce, he and his mother remained in Toronto; his father returned to Memphis, where he was incarcerated for a number of years on drug-related charges.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-26)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] Graham's limited finances and legal issues caused him to remain in the US until Drake's early adulthood. Prior to his arrest, Graham would travel to Toronto and bring Drake to Memphis every summer.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-27)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Complex-28)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-29) Graham claimed in an interview that Drake's assertions of him being an absent father were embellishments used to sell music,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-30) which Drake vehemently denies.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-31)
Drake was raised in two neighbourhoods. He lived on [Weston Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weston_Road "Weston Road") in Toronto's working-class west end until grade six and attended Weston Memorial Junior Public School until grade four, playing [minor hockey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minor_hockey "Minor hockey") with the [Weston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weston,_Toronto "Weston, Toronto") Red Wings. Drake was a promising right [winger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winger_\(ice_hockey\) "Winger \(ice hockey\)"), reaching the [Upper Canada College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Canada_College "Upper Canada College") hockey camp, but left at the behest of his mother following a vicious [cross-check](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-checking "Cross-checking") to his neck during a game by an opposing player.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Complex-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-32) He moved to one of the city's affluent neighbourhoods, [Forest Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Hill,_Toronto "Forest Hill, Toronto"), in 2000.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-toronto-33)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-torstar09-34) When asked about the move, Drake replied, "[We had] a half of a house we could live in. The other people had the top half, we had the bottom half. I lived in the basement, my mom lived on the first floor. It was not big, it was not luxurious. It was what we could afford."[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-35) At age 10, Drake appeared in a comedic sketch which aired during the 1997 NHL Awards, featuring a riff of [Martin Brodeur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Brodeur "Martin Brodeur") and [Ron Hextall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Hextall "Ron Hextall") and their record as being the only goalies to have scored multiple goals.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-36)
He attended [Forest Hill Collegiate Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Hill_Collegiate_Institute "Forest Hill Collegiate Institute") for high school,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Graham1-37) and attended [Vaughan Road Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaughan_Road_Academy "Vaughan Road Academy") in Toronto's multicultural [Oakwood–Vaughan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakwood%E2%80%93Vaughan "Oakwood–Vaughan") neighbourhood; Drake described Vaughan Road Academy as "not by any means the easiest school to go to".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Complex-28) During his teenage years, Drake worked at a now-closed Toronto furniture factory owned by his maternal grandfather, Reuben Sher.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-38) Drake said he was bullied at school for his racial and religious background,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-39) and upon determining that his class schedule was detrimental to his burgeoning acting career, he dropped out of school.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Vibe_Interview-40) Drake received his [high school diploma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Educational_Development "General Educational Development") in October 2012 at age 25.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-41)
## Career
### 2001–2009: Career beginnings
At 15, Drake was introduced to a high school friend's father, an acting agent. He found Drake a role on the Canadian [teen drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_drama "Teen drama") series _[Degrassi: The Next Generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Degrassi:_The_Next_Generation "Degrassi: The Next Generation")_ , in which Drake portrayed [Jimmy Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Brooks "Jimmy Brooks"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Post-42) a basketball star who became physically disabled after he was shot by a classmate. When asked about his early acting career, Drake replied, "My mother was very sick. We were very poor, like broke. The only money I had coming in was [from] Canadian TV."[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Complex-28) According to showrunners [Linda Schuyler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Schuyler "Linda Schuyler") and [Stephen Stohn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Stohn "Stephen Stohn"), Drake regularly arrived late on set after spending nights recording music. To prevent this, Schuyler claimed Drake struck an agreement with the set's security guards to gain entry to the set after recording to be allowed to sleep in a dressing room.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-43) Drake's first recorded song, "Do What You Do", appeared on _[The N Soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_N_Soundtrack "The N Soundtrack")_ , which was released by [The N](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_N "The N") (the night-time block for [Noggin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noggin_\(brand\) "Noggin \(brand\)")), as it was the network that the series was airing on in the United States.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-noggin-press-44)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Lil_Wayne_in_Concert.jpg/250px-Lil_Wayne_in_Concert.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lil_Wayne_in_Concert.jpg)[Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne"), the founder of [Young Money Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Money_Entertainment "Young Money Entertainment"), signed Drake to the label in 2009.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-45)
During his early career, Graham co-formed the R&B duo The Renaissance with singer [Melanie Fiona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melanie_Fiona "Melanie Fiona"), although not releasing an album. Being musically inspired by [Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z") and [Clipse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clipse "Clipse"), Drake [self-released](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-released "Self-released") his debut [mixtape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixtape "Mixtape"), _[Room for Improvement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Room_for_Improvement_\(mixtape\) "Room for Improvement \(mixtape\)")_ featuring [Trey Songz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trey_Songz "Trey Songz") and [Lupe Fiasco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lupe_Fiasco "Lupe Fiasco"), in 2006. Drake described the project as "pretty straightforward, radio friendly, [and] not much content to it". _Room for Improvement_ was released for sale only and sold roughly 6,000 copies,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Post-42) for which Drake received [$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_dollar "Canadian dollar")304.04 in [royalties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royalties "Royalties").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-46) He performed his first concert on August 19, 2006, at the [Kool Haus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kool_Haus "Kool Haus") nightclub as an [opening act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opening_act "Opening act") for [Ice Cube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_Cube "Ice Cube"), performing for half an hour and earning $100.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-47) In 2007, Drake released his second mixtape _[Comeback Season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comeback_Season_\(mixtape\) "Comeback Season \(mixtape\)")_. Released from his recently founded [October's Very Own](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October's_Very_Own "October's Very Own") label, it spawned the single "Replacement Girl" featuring Trey Songz.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-48) The song sampled "Man of the Year" by [Brisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisco_\(rapper\) "Brisco \(rapper\)"), [Flo Rida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flo_Rida "Flo Rida"), and [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne"), retaining Lil Wayne's verse; the rapper invited Drake to [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston") to join his _[Tha Carter III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tha_Carter_III "Tha Carter III")_ tour. On tour, Drake and Lil Wayne recorded multiple songs together, including "Ransom", "[Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forever_\(Drake,_Kanye_West,_Lil_Wayne,_and_Eminem_song\) "Forever \(Drake, Kanye West, Lil Wayne, and Eminem song\)")", and a remix to "Brand New".[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Fader-49)
In 2009, Drake released his third mixtape _[So Far Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So_Far_Gone_\(mixtape\) "So Far Gone \(mixtape\)")_. It was made available for free download through his OVO blog website, and featured Lil Wayne, Trey Songz, [Omarion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omarion "Omarion"), [Lloyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_\(singer\) "Lloyd \(singer\)"), and [Bun B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bun_B "Bun B"). It received over 2,000 downloads in the first 2 hours of release, finding mainstream commercial success from the singles "[Best I Ever Had](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_I_Ever_Had "Best I Ever Had")" and "[Successful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Successful_\(song\) "Successful \(song\)")", both gaining Platinum certification by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA), with the former also peaking at number two on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-50) This prompted the mixtape's re-release as an [EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So_Far_Gone_\(EP\) "So Far Gone \(EP\)"), featuring four songs from the original, as well as the additions of the songs "[I'm Goin' In](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Goin'_In "I'm Goin' In")" and "Fear". It debuted at number six on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), and won the Rap Recording of the Year at the [2010 Juno Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Juno_Awards "2010 Juno Awards").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-51)
Due to the success of the mixtape,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-52) Drake was the subject of a bidding war from various labels, often reported as "one of the biggest bidding wars ever".[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-53) He had secured a recording contract with Young Money Entertainment on June 29, 2009.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-54) Drake joined the rest of the label's roster on the America's Most Wanted Tour in July 2009.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-55) However, during a performance of "Best I Ever Had" in [Camden, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camden,_New_Jersey "Camden, New Jersey"), Drake fell on stage and tore the [anterior cruciate ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_cruciate_ligament "Anterior cruciate ligament") in his right knee.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-56)
In 2009 The Nightingale Company, the studio of television producer [Debbie Nightingale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debbie_Nightingale "Debbie Nightingale"), announced the development of _Us and Them_ , a television comedy series which would have starred Graham and his _Degrassi_ castmate [Mazin Elsadig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazin_Elsadig "Mazin Elsadig"),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-57) although the series was never completed.
### 2010–2012: Musical breakthrough with _Thank Me Later_ and _Take Care_
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Drake_2010.jpg/250px-Drake_2010.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Drake_2010.jpg)Drake at [Bumbershoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bumbershoot "Bumbershoot") in 2010
Drake planned to release his debut album, _[Thank Me Later](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank_Me_Later "Thank Me Later")_ , in late 2008, but the album's release date was thrice postponed up to June 15, 2010.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-lightup-58)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-59) On March 9, 2010, Drake released the lead single "[Over](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Over_\(Drake_song\) "Over \(Drake song\)")",[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-60) which peaked at number fourteen on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, as well as topping the [Rap Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap_Songs "Rap Songs") chart. It received a nomination for [Best Rap Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Rap_Solo_Performance "Best Rap Solo Performance") at the [53rd Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/53rd_Grammy_Awards "53rd Grammy Awards").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-OVERBILL-61) His second single, "[Find Your Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Find_Your_Love "Find Your Love")", became a bigger success. It peaked at number five on the Hot 100, and was certified [3× Multi-Platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_certification "Platinum certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA).[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-62) The music video for the single was shot in [Kingston, Jamaica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingston,_Jamaica "Kingston, Jamaica"), and was criticized by Jamaica's minister of tourism [Edmund Bartlett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_Bartlett "Edmund Bartlett").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-63) The third single and fourth singles, "[Miss Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_Me "Miss Me")" and "[Fancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fancy_\(Drake_song\) "Fancy \(Drake song\)")" respectively,[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-64) attained moderate commercial success; however, the latter garnered Drake his second nomination at the 53rd Grammy Awards for [Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Rap_Performance_by_a_Duo_or_Group "Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-65)
_Thank Me Later_ was released on June 15, 2010,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-66) debuting at number one on the _Billboard_ 200 with sales of over 447,000 copies in its first week.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-67) Upon the album's release, 25,000 fans gathered at New York City's South Street Seaport for a free concert hosted by Drake and [Hanson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanson_\(band\) "Hanson \(band\)"), which was later cancelled by the police after a near-riot ensued due to overflowing crowds.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-68) The album became the top selling debut album for any artist in 2010 and had the highest sales week for any debut album in the 2010s[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-69) and featured Lil Wayne, [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West"),[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-70) and Jay Z.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Hip-Hop_Since_1978:_Official_Site-71) Drake began his [Away from Home Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_from_Home_Tour "Away from Home Tour") on September 20, 2010, in Miami, Florida, performing at 78 shows over four different legs.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-72) It concluded in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Valley "Las Vegas Valley") in November 2010.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-73) Due to the tour's success, Drake hosted the first OVO Festival in 2010. Drake had an eco-friendly college tour to support the album.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Eco-74)
Drake announced his intentions to allow [Noah "40" Shebib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_"40"_Shebib "Noah "40" Shebib") to record a more cohesive sound on his next album than on _Thank Me Later_.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Jones-75) In November 2010, Drake revealed the title of his next studio album would be _Take Care_.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-TakeCare-76) He sought to expand on the low-tempo, sensuous, and dark sonic esthetic of _Thank Me Later_.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-soulculture.co.uk-77)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-autogenerated1-78) Primarily a [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop") album, Drake also attempted to incorporate [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R&B "R&B") and pop to create a languid, grandiose sound.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Frere-Jones-79)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Drake_at_Bun-B_Concert_2011_%281%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Drake_at_Bun-B_Concert_2011_%281%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Drake_at_Bun-B_Concert_2011_\(1\)_\(cropped\).jpg)Drake performing in 2011
In January 2011, Drake was in negotiations to join [Eva Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eva_Green "Eva Green") and [Susan Sarandon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Sarandon "Susan Sarandon") as a member of the cast in [Nicholas Jarecki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Jarecki "Nicholas Jarecki")'s _[Arbitrage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arbitrage_\(film\) "Arbitrage \(film\)")_ ,[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-80) before ultimately deciding against starring in the movie to focus on the album. "Dreams Money Can Buy"[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-81) and "[Marvins Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvins_Room "Marvins Room")"[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-soulculture.co.uk-77) were released on Drake's October's Very Own Blog, on May 20 and June 9, respectively. Acting as promotional singles for _Take Care_ , the former was eventually unincluded on the album's final track listing, while "Marvins Room" gained [3× Multi-Platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_sales_certification "Music recording sales certification") certification by the RIAA,[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-82) as well as peaking at number 21 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Drake-83) "[Headlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headlines_\(Drake_song\) "Headlines \(Drake song\)")" was released on August 9 as the album's lead single. It met with positive critical and commercial response, reaching number thirteen on the Hot 100, as well as becoming Drake's tenth single to reach the summit of the _Billboard_ [Hot Rap Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Rap_Songs "Hot Rap Songs").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-84) It was eventually certified 4× Multi-Platinum in the United States and Platinum in Canada.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-85) The music video for the single was released on October 2.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-86)
_Take Care_ was released on November 15, 2011, and received generally positive reviews from [music critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_criticism "Music criticism").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-CBS_Interactive-87)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-McDonnell-88)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Dombal-89)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Hutchins-90)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Kot-91) It also won the [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") for [Best Rap Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Rap_Album "Best Rap Album") at the [55th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "55th Annual Grammy Awards"), and achieved great commercial success, eventually being certified six times platinum by the RIAA in 2019, with sales for the album marking 2.6 million in the US[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-billboard_aug2015-92) The album's third and fourth singles, "[The Motto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Motto_\(Drake_song\) "The Motto \(Drake song\)")" and [Take Care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take_Care_\(song\) "Take Care \(song\)")", were released on November 29, 2011[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-RIAA-93) and February 21, 2012, respectively.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-94) Each song achieved commercial success, and "The Motto" was later credited for [popularizing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#Public_image) the phrase "[YOLO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YOLO_\(motto\) "YOLO \(motto\)")" in the United States.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-YOLO-95)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-96) The music video for "Take Care" met with widespread acclaim,[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-97) receiving four nominations at the [2012 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2012 MTV Video Music Awards"), including for [Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Video of the Year").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-98) "[HYFR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HYFR "HYFR")" was the final single to be released from the album, and became certified 2× Multi-Platinum.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-99)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-100)
On August 5, 2012, Drake released "[Enough Said](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enough_Said_\(song\) "Enough Said \(song\)")", performed by [Aaliyah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaliyah "Aaliyah") and himself.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-bb-101) Originally recorded prior to [Aaliyah's 2001 death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_Aaliyah "Death of Aaliyah"), Drake later finished the track with producer "40".[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-mtv-102) In promotion of his second album, Drake embarked on the worldwide [Club Paradise Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Paradise_Tour "Club Paradise Tour"). It became the most successful hip-hop tour of 2012, grossing over $42 million.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-103) He then returned to acting, starring in _[Ice Age: Continental Drift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_Age:_Continental_Drift "Ice Age: Continental Drift")_ as [Ethan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Ice_Age_characters#Ethan "List of Ice Age characters").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-104)
### 2013–2015: _Nothing Was the Same_ and _If You're Reading This It's Too Late_
By the [Club Paradise Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Paradise_Tour "Club Paradise Tour")'s European leg, Drake had begun working on his third studio album, which he said would retain 40 as the album's executive producer, include the influence of British producer [Jamie xx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_xx "Jamie xx"),[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-105) and stylistically differ from _Take Care_ , departing from the ambient production and despondent lyrics previously prevalent.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-106) After he won the [Grammy Award for Best Rap Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Album "Grammy Award for Best Rap Album") at the [55th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "55th Annual Grammy Awards") on February 10, 2013, Drake announced his third album, _[Nothing Was the Same](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nothing_Was_the_Same "Nothing Was the Same")_ , and released its [first single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Started_from_the_Bottom "Started from the Bottom").[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-107) The album's second single, "[Hold On, We're Going Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hold_On,_We're_Going_Home "Hold On, We're Going Home")", was released in August, peaking at number one on the _Billboard_ Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-108) _Nothing Was the Same_ was released on September 24, 2013, debuting at number one on the US _Billboard_ 200, with 658,000 copies sold in its first week of release.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-109) The album debuted atop the charts in Canada, Denmark, Australia and the United Kingdom. The album also enjoyed generally favourable reviews by contemporary music critics, commending the musical shift in terms of the tone and subject matter, comparing it to Kanye West's _[808s& Heartbreak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/808s_&_Heartbreak "808s & Heartbreak")_.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-shortlist-110)
The album, which sold over 1,720,000 copies in the United States, was further promoted by the "[Would You like a Tour?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Would_You_like_a_Tour%3F "Would You like a Tour?")" throughout late 2013 to early 2014.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-111) It became the 22nd-most successful tour of the year, grossing an estimated $46 million.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-112) Drake then returned to acting in January 2014, hosting _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")_ , as well as serving as the musical guest. His versatility, acting ability and comedic timing were all praised by critics, describing it as what "kept him afloat during the tough and murky SNL waters".[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-SNL-113)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-114)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:6-115)
In late 2014, Drake announced that he began recording sessions for his fourth studio album.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-116) On February 12, 2015, Drake released _[If You're Reading This It's Too Late](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_You're_Reading_This_It's_Too_Late "If You're Reading This It's Too Late")_ onto [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes") with no prior announcement. Despite debate on whether it was an album[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-117) or a mixtape,[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-118) its commercial stance quantifies it as his fourth retail project with [Cash Money Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cash_Money_Records "Cash Money Records"), a scheme that was rumoured to allow Drake to leave the label.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-119)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-120) However, he eventually remained with Cash Money, and _If You're Reading This It's Too Late_ sold over 1 million units in 2015.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-billboard_aug2015-92)
### 2015–2017: _What a Time to Be Alive_ , _Views_ , and _More Life_
On July 31, 2015, Drake released four singles: "[Back to Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_to_Back_\(Drake_song\) "Back to Back \(Drake song\)")", "[Charged Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charged_Up "Charged Up")", "[Hotline Bling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotline_Bling "Hotline Bling")", and "[Right Hand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_Hand_\(song\) "Right Hand \(song\)")". On September 20, Drake released a [collaborative mixtape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_a_Time_to_Be_Alive "What a Time to Be Alive") with [Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_\(rapper\) "Future \(rapper\)"),[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-121)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-122) which was recorded in [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta") in just under a week.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-123) _What a Time to Be Alive_ debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ 200, making Drake the first hip-hop artist to have two projects reach number one in the same year [since 2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Black_Album_\(Jay-Z_album\) "The Black Album \(Jay-Z album\)").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-124) It was later certified [2× multi platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) for combined sales, streaming and track-sales equivalent of over 2 million units.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-125) Drake announced in January 2016 that his fourth studio album would be launched during the spring, releasing the [promotional single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotional_single "Promotional single") "[Summer Sixteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Sixteen "Summer Sixteen")" later that month. The album was originally titled _Views from the 6_ , but was later shortened to _Views_.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Singelton-126)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Drake_July_2016.jpg/250px-Drake_July_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Drake_July_2016.jpg)Drake performing at the [Summer Sixteen Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Sixteen_Tour "Summer Sixteen Tour") in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto") in 2016
"Summer Sixteen" debuted at number six on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100, and proved controversial—Drake's self-comparisons with more tenured artists divided many critics, who described his self-comparison as "goodly brash" or "conventionally disrespectful".[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-127)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-128)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-129) Drake soon released the album's lead singles, "[Pop Style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Style "Pop Style")" and the [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall")-infused "[One Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Dance "One Dance")", on April 5. Both debuted within the top 40 of the _Billboard_ Hot 100;[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-130) however, the latter proved more commercially successful, with "One Dance" becoming Drake's first number-one single in Canada and the US as a leading artist.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-131)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-132) The single also became Drake's first number one single as a lead artist in the United Kingdom, and peaked at number one in many other countries.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-133)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-134) _[Views](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Views_\(album\) "Views \(album\)")_ was previewed in London before its premiere a day later. It was released as an [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") and [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes") exclusive on April 29 before being made available to various other platforms later that week.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-135)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-136) _Views_ would become Drake's most commercially successful album, sitting atop the _Billboard_ 200 for thirteen weeks, as well as simultaneously leading the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and the _Billboard_ 200 for eight weeks. It achieved sextuple-platinum status in the US, and earned over 1 million [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") in the first week of its release, as well as gaining over half-billion overall streams.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Rolling_Stone-137)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-BillboardViews-138)[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-139) Despite its success, critical reception was mixed: the album drew criticism for its length, lack of a cohesive theme, and dearth of artistic challenge.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-inq-140)
Drake returned to host _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")_ on May 14, serving as the show's musical guest.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-141) Drake and [Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_\(rapper\) "Future \(rapper\)") then announced the [Summer Sixteen Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Sixteen_Tour "Summer Sixteen Tour") to showcase their collective mixtape, as well as their respective studio albums.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-142) The latter dates of the tour were postponed due to Drake suffering an ankle injury.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-143) According to _[Pollstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollstar "Pollstar")_ , the Summer Sixteen Tour was the highest grossing hip-hop tour of all time, having earnt $84.3 million across 56 dates.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-144) On July 23, Drake announced that he was working on a new project, scheduled to be released in early 2017.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-145)
During the 2016 OVO Festival, Kanye West confirmed that he and Drake had begun working on a collaborative album.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-146) Soon after, the music video for "Child's Play" was released.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-147) On September 26, _Please Forgive Me_ was released as an Apple Music exclusive. It ran a total of 25 minutes, and featured music from _Views_.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-148) At the [2016 BET Hip-Hop Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_BET_Hip_Hop_Awards "2016 BET Hip Hop Awards"), Drake received the most nominations, with 10,[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-149) winning the awards for Album of the Year and Best Hip-Hop Video.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-150)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-151) Drake later announced the [Boy Meets World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Meets_World_Tour "Boy Meets World Tour") on October 10.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-152)
During an episode of OVO Sound Radio, Drake confirmed he would be releasing a project titled _[More Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/More_Life "More Life")_ , described as a "playlist of original music".[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-153) Drake later secured his second and third Grammy Awards, winning for [Best Rap/Sung Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Rap/Sung_Performance "Best Rap/Sung Performance") and [Best Rap Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Rap_Song "Best Rap Song") at the [59th ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "59th Annual Grammy Awards").[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-auto-154) Upon release on March 18, 2017, _More Life_ received mostly positive reviews, and debuted atop the _Billboard_ 200, earning 505,000 [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") in its first week.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-More_Life_Billboard-155) It also set a streaming record, becoming the highest ever streamed album in 24 hours, with a total of 89.9 million streams on Apple Music and 61.3 million on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify").[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-156) He later won a record 13 awards at the [2017 Billboard Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Billboard_Music_Awards "2017 Billboard Music Awards") in May.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-chicagotribune-157) By this time, Drake had been present on the _Hot 100_ chart for eight consecutive years, and had the most recorded entries by a solo artist.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-158) Drake hosted the [first annual NBA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_NBA_Awards "2017 NBA Awards") on June 26,[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-159) and also appeared in _[The Carter Effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Carter_Effect "The Carter Effect")_ documentary.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-usacartereffect-160)
### 2018–2019: _Scary Hours_ , _Scorpion_ , and _Care Package_ ; return to television
Drake released a mini EP titled _[Scary Hours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scary_Hours "Scary Hours")_ on January 20, 2018, marking Drake's first solo release since _More Life_.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-161) _Scary Hours_ featured the songs "[Diplomatic Immunity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_Immunity_\(song\) "Diplomatic Immunity \(song\)")" and "[God's Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God's_Plan_\(song\) "God's Plan \(song\)")", with the latter debuting at number one on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Billboard-162)[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-163)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-164) The song was Drake's first song as a solo artist to reach number one. It also became his first song to be certified Diamond by the RIAA,[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-165) and it is currently tied for the fourth highest certified digital single ever in the US[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-166) He was later featured on [BlocBoy JB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BlocBoy_JB "BlocBoy JB")'s February 2018 debut single "[Look Alive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Look_Alive_\(BlocBoy_JB_song\) "Look Alive \(BlocBoy JB song\)")".[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-167) The song's entry on the Hot 100 made Drake the rapper with the most top 10 hits on the Hot 100, with 23.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-168)
On April 6, "[Nice for What](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nice_for_What "Nice for What")", a single from his fifth studio album, was released.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-169)[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-170) It replaced his own "God's Plan" on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 at number one, making Drake the first artist to have a new number-one debut replace their former number-one debut. He then announced the title of his fifth studio album as _[Scorpion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorpion_\(Drake_album\) "Scorpion \(Drake album\)")_ , with a planned release date of June 29, 2018.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-171)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-172) "[I'm Upset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Upset "I'm Upset")" was released on May 26 as the album's third single.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-173) _Scorpion_ was Drake's longest project, with a run-time of just under 90 minutes. The album broke both the one-day global records on Spotify and Apple Music, as it gained 132.45 million and 170 million plays on each streaming service, respectively.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-auto2-174) It eventually sold 749,000 album equivalent units in its first week of sales, and debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ 200.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-175)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-176)
Drake earned his sixth US number-one with "[In My Feelings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Feelings "In My Feelings")" on July 21.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-177) The success of "In My Feelings" also made Drake the record holder for most number one hits among rappers.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-178) He then appeared on the [Travis Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travis_Scott "Travis Scott") album _[Astroworld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astroworld_\(album\) "Astroworld \(album\)")_ , featuring vocals for the song "[Sicko Mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sicko_Mode "Sicko Mode")", which peaked at number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-179)[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Sicko_mode-12) Drake announced in July 2018 that he planned to "take 6 months to a year" to himself to return to television and films, producing the television series _[Euphoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphoria_\(American_TV_series\) "Euphoria \(American TV series\)")_ and _[Top Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Boy "Top Boy")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:4-16) He then began the [Aubrey & the Three Migos Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aubrey_&_the_Three_Migos_Tour "Aubrey & the Three Migos Tour") with co-headliners [Migos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Migos "Migos") on August 12. This preceded a collaboration with [Bad Bunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Bunny "Bad Bunny") titled "[Mia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mia_\(Bad_Bunny_song\) "Mia \(Bad Bunny song\)")", which featured Drake performing in Spanish.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-180)
In February 2019, he received his fourth [Grammy Award for Best Rap Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rap_Song "Grammy Award for Best Rap Song"), for "God's Plan", at the [61st Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/61st_Annual_Grammy_Awards "61st Annual Grammy Awards").[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-181) During his speech, producers abruptly cut to a commercial break, leading viewers to speculate they were censoring his speech during which he criticized [The Recording Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Recording_Academy "The Recording Academy").[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-182) A legal representative for the academy released a statement stating "a natural pause [led] the producers [to] assume that he was done and cut to commercial", and added the organization offered him an opportunity to return to stage, but he declined.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-183)
On February 14, Drake re-released his third mixtape, _[So Far Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So_Far_Gone_\(mixtape\) "So Far Gone \(mixtape\)")_ , onto streaming services for the first time to commemorate its 10-year anniversary.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-184) On June 15, Drake released two songs, "[Omertà](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omert%C3%A0_\(Drake_song\) "Omertà \(Drake song\)")" and "[Money in the Grave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money_in_the_Grave "Money in the Grave")", on his EP _[The Best in the World Pack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Best_in_the_World_Pack "The Best in the World Pack")_ to celebrate the [NBA Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NBA_Finals "2019 NBA Finals") win of the [Toronto Raptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Raptors "Toronto Raptors").[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-185) On August 2, he released the compilation album _[Care Package](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Care_Package_\(album\) "Care Package \(album\)")_ , consisting of songs released between 2010 and 2016 that were initially unavailable for purchase or commercial streaming;[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-186) it debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ 200 with 109,000 album equivalent units in its first week of sales.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-187)
### 2019–2021: _Dark Lane Demo Tapes_ , _Scary Hours 2_ , and _Certified Lover Boy_
Drake released the song "[War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_\(Drake_song\) "War \(Drake song\)")" on December 24, 2019, which was widely noted for its [UK drill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_drill "UK drill")-inspired instrumental.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-188)[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-189)[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:0-190) The following day, he revealed that he was in the process of completing his sixth studio album.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-191) On April 3, he released "[Toosie Slide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toosie_Slide "Toosie Slide")" with a music video, which features a dance created in collaboration with social media influencer Toosie.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-192) It debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, making Drake the first male artist to have three songs debut at number one.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-193) On May 1, 2020, Drake released the commercial mixtape _[Dark Lane Demo Tapes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_Lane_Demo_Tapes "Dark Lane Demo Tapes")_ , with guest appearances from [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown "Chris Brown"), Future, [Young Thug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Thug "Young Thug"), [Fivio Foreign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fivio_Foreign "Fivio Foreign"), [Playboi Carti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playboi_Carti "Playboi Carti"), and Sosa Geek.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-194) The mixtape is a compilation of new songs and tracks that leaked on the internet.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-195) It received mixed reviews and debuted at number two on the US _Billboard_ 200,[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-BB200-196) and at number one on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart").[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-197)
Drake also announced that his sixth studio album would be released in the summer of 2020.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-198) On August 14, "[Laugh Now Cry Later](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laugh_Now_Cry_Later "Laugh Now Cry Later")" featuring [Lil Durk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Durk "Lil Durk") was released, which was intended as the lead single from the upcoming album _[Certified Lover Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Lover_Boy "Certified Lover Boy")_ ,[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-199) but not included on the final track listing. It debuted at number two on the Hot 100, and was nominated for [Best Rap Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Rap_Song "Best Rap Song") at the [63rd Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/63rd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "63rd Annual Grammy Awards"). On his 34th birthday, Drake announced _Certified Lover Boy_ was set to be released in January 2021.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-january-200)[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-201) This was later pushed back after he sustained a serious knee injury.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-202)
In January 2021, Drake became the first artist to surpass 50 billion combined streams on Spotify.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-203) On March 5, Drake released an EP titled _[Scary Hours 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scary_Hours_2 "Scary Hours 2")_ , which includes three songs: "[What's Next](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What's_Next_\(Drake_song\) "What's Next \(Drake song\)")", "[Wants and Needs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wants_and_Needs "Wants and Needs")" with [Lil Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Baby "Lil Baby"), and "Lemon Pepper Freestyle" with [Rick Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Ross "Rick Ross").[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-204) These three songs entered the charts at numbers one, two, and three, respectively, making Drake the first artist to have three songs debut in the top three on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-205) He was named [Artist of the Decade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Artist_of_the_Decade_Award "Billboard Artist of the Decade Award") at the [2021 _Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Billboard_Music_Awards "2021 Billboard Music Awards").[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:2-206)
_[Certified Lover Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Lover_Boy "Certified Lover Boy")_ was released on September 3, 2021, becoming Drake's tenth number-one album on the _Billboard_ 200;[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-207) every song debuted on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, while the album was the first to chart nine songs in the top 10, with "[Way 2 Sexy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Way_2_Sexy "Way 2 Sexy")" becoming Drake's ninth number-one single.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-top_40_entries-208)[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-billboard_drake-209) _Certified Lover Boy_ was nominated for [Best Rap Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Rap_Album "Best Rap Album") and "Way 2 Sexy" was nominated for [Best Rap Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Rap_Performance "Best Rap Performance") at the [64th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/64th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "64th Annual Grammy Awards").[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-210) He was later named _Billboard_ 's [Top Artist of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Top_Artist "Billboard Year-End Top Artist") for 2021,[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-211) and was the fourth most streamed artist on Spotify for the year, and the most streamed rapper.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-212) On December 6, he withdrew his music for consideration for the Grammys, with multiple outlets noting his contentious relationship with the Recording Academy.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-horton1-213) Drake accumulated 8.6 billion on-demand streams in 2021, making him the most overall streamed artist of the year in the United States; one out of every 131 streams was a Drake song.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-214)
### 2022–2024: _Honestly, Nevermind_ , _Her Loss_ , _For All the Dogs_ , Kendrick Lamar feud, and _100 Gigs_
On March 3, 2022, Drake placed fourth on _Forbes_ 's ranking of highest paid rappers of 2021, with an estimated pre-tax income of $50 million.[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-215) On April 16, it was calculated Drake generated more streams in 2021 than every song released prior to 1980 combined; his music accumulated 7.91 billion streams, while songs pre-1980 had generated 6.32 billion.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-216) Drake was then confirmed as a guest artist on Future's _[I Never Liked You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Never_Liked_You_\(album\) "I Never Liked You \(album\)")_ (2022); one of the songs he featured on, "[Wait for U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wait_for_U "Wait for U")", debuted atop the _Billboard_ Hot 100, becoming Drake's tenth number-one song and making him the tenth act to achieve ten number ones.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-217)
In early May, Drake re-signed with [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group") in a multifaceted deal reported to be worth as much as $400 million, making it one of the largest recording contracts ever.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-218) On June 16, Drake announced his seventh album, _[Honestly, Nevermind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honestly,_Nevermind "Honestly, Nevermind")_ , which released a day later; he also announced a third iteration of his _[Scary Hours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scary_Hours "Scary Hours")_ [EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EP "EP") series.[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-219) _Honestly, Nevermind_ sold 204,000 [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") in its first week, becoming Drake's eleventh US number-one album and making him the fifth artist with over 10 number one albums, after [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") (19), Jay-Z (14), [Bruce Springsteen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Springsteen "Bruce Springsteen"), and [Barbra Streisand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbra_Streisand "Barbra Streisand") (both 11).[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-220) "[Jimmy Cooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Cooks "Jimmy Cooks")" also became Drake's eleventh US number-one song.[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-221)
On July 14, it was announced Drake would reunite with Lil Wayne and [Nicki Minaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicki_Minaj "Nicki Minaj") on a [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto") exclusive concert series on July 28, July 29, and August 1.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-222) After the debut of "Staying Alive" on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100, it marked the 30th Drake song to reach the top five on the chart, breaking a 55-year-old record for most songs to reach the top five on the chart (29), held by the Beatles.[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-223) Drake refused to submit his music for Grammy consideration for a second consecutive year.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-224) On October 22, Drake announced _[Her Loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_Loss "Her Loss")_ , a collaborative album with [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage "21 Savage") which would release on October 28;[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-225) it was then delayed to November 4 after Drake's longtime producer, [40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40_\(record_producer\) "40 \(record producer\)"), was diagnosed with COVID-19.[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-226) _Her Loss_ debuted atop the _Billboard_ 200, accumulating first week sales of 404,000 album-equivalent units. Eight of the album's songs debuted in the top ten on the _Billboard_ Hot 100, extending Drake's record for most top ten entries, with 67 (with a record 49 as a lead artist).[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-8_Songs-227) On November 15, Drake was nominated for four awards at the [2023 Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Grammy_Awards "2023 Grammy Awards"), including [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") for his writing on Beyoncé's _Renaissance_.[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-228) In February 2023, Drake was named the most streamed act ever on Spotify.[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-229)
On July 23, via an announcement for his poetry book _Titles Ruin Everything_ , Drake announced his eighth studio album, titled _[For All the Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs "For All the Dogs")_.[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-230) On September 15, Drake released the lead single of the album, "[Slime You Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slime_You_Out "Slime You Out")", featuring [SZA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SZA "SZA").[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-231) The song charted at number one on the US _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-232) On October 5, Drake released the album's second single, "[8AM in Charlotte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8AM_in_Charlotte "8AM in Charlotte")", on his social media accounts.[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-single3-233) On October 6, Drake released _For All The Dogs_ , which debuted atop the _Billboard_ 200, accumulating first week sales of 402,000 album-equivalent units.[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-234) The album also debuted seven tracks in the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100, with "[First Person Shooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Person_Shooter_\(song\) "First Person Shooter \(song\)")" featuring [J. Cole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Cole "J. Cole") topping the chart, tying Drake with [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson") for the most solo number-one songs by a solo male artist.[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-235)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0b/KendrickSZASPurs230725-21_-_54683275585_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-KendrickSZASPurs230725-21_-_54683275585_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:KendrickSZASPurs230725-21_-_54683275585_\(cropped\).jpg)In 2024, he was involved in a [rap feud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap_feud "Rap feud") with [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") (_pictured_).
On March 22, Kendrick Lamar dissed Drake, as well as J. Cole, on Future and Metro Boomin's song "[Like That](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Like_That_\(Future,_Metro_Boomin_and_Kendrick_Lamar_song\) "Like That \(Future, Metro Boomin and Kendrick Lamar song\)")", beginning [a feud between them](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake%E2%80%93Kendrick_Lamar_feud "Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud").[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-236) On April 19, Drake released "[Push Ups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push_Ups_\(song\) "Push Ups \(song\)")" after early versions were leaked online as a response track while also addressing Future and Rick Ross, followed up with "[Taylor Made Freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Made_Freestyle "Taylor Made Freestyle")" later that day. On April 30, Lamar released a diss track named "[Euphoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphoria_\(Kendrick_Lamar_song\) "Euphoria \(Kendrick Lamar song\)")" in response, as well as "[6:16 in LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6:16_in_LA "6:16 in LA")" on May 3, exclusively on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"). That same day, Drake released "[Family Matters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Matters_\(Drake_song\) "Family Matters \(Drake song\)")" exclusively on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") in response. Lamar released "[Meet the Grahams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet_the_Grahams "Meet the Grahams")" 20 minutes later, and would go onto release "[Not Like Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us "Not Like Us")" the following day.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-237) On May 5, Drake released "[The Heart Part 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Heart_Part_6 "The Heart Part 6")", a reference to Lamar's "The Heart" song series.[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-238)
### 2025–present: _Some Sexy Songs 4 U_ , _Iceman_ , _Maid of Honour_ , _Habibti_ and _Fear of Missing Out_
On February 3, 2025, Drake announced _[Some Sexy Songs 4 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some_Sexy_Songs_4_U "Some Sexy Songs 4 U")_ , a collaborative album with [PartyNextDoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PartyNextDoor "PartyNextDoor"), which was released on February 14, 2025.[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-239)[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-240)[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-241) _$ome $exy $ongs 4 U_ debuted at number one on the _Billboard_ 200 chart, tying the _Billboard_ record for most number one albums by a solo artist.[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-242) On February 16, it was announced that Drake would be the first artist in history to headline all three days at the 2025 [Wireless Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wireless_Festival "Wireless Festival"). Drake became the fastest artist to sell out the festival in its history, selling all tickets in minutes.[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-243) Directly after the festival, he commenced his [Some Special Shows 4 U](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Some_Special_Shows_4_U "Some Special Shows 4 U") tour in Europe, which concluded on September 23.[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-244)
On July 5, 2025, Drake released the single "[What Did I Miss?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What_Did_I_Miss%3F "What Did I Miss?")" as the lead single of his upcoming ninth studio album, _[Iceman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iceman_\(Drake_album\) "Iceman \(Drake album\)")_. It marks his return to solo material.[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-245) On May 14, 2026 it was announced that alongside _Iceman_ , two new albums entitled _[Habibti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habibti_\(album\) "Habibti \(album\)")_ and _[Maid of Honour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maid_of_Honour_\(album\) "Maid of Honour \(album\)")_ would be released the following day. They debuted at, respectively, numbers one, two, and three on the _Billboard_ 200 chart, making Drake the first artist to hold the top three positions concurrently.[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-246)
In September 2026, Drake expanded his production on cinema with the release of _[Fear of Missing Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear_of_Missing_Out "Fear of Missing Out")_ (stylized as _FOMO_), a "not so short film".[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-rollingstoneFOMO-247) The film premiered on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), following a rollout that included teaser campaigns and photo drops.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-hiphopcanada-248)
## Artistry
### Influences
Drake has cited several [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop") artists as influencing his [rapping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapping "Rapping") style, including Kanye West,[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-249) Jay-Z,[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-250) [MF Doom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MF_Doom "MF Doom"),[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-251) and Lil Wayne,[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-252) while also attributing various [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") artists as influential to the incorporation of the genre into his own music, including [Aaliyah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaliyah "Aaliyah")[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Soul_Train-253) and [Usher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usher_\(musician\) "Usher \(musician\)").[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-254) Drake has also credited several [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall") artists for later influencing his [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_music "Caribbean music")-inflected style, including [Vybz Kartel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vybz_Kartel "Vybz Kartel"), whom he has called one of his "biggest inspirations".[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-255)[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:1-256)
### Musical style
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Kanye_West_by_David_Shankbone_%283465084618%29.jpg/250px-Kanye_West_by_David_Shankbone_%283465084618%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kanye_West_by_David_Shankbone_\(3465084618\).jpg)
