[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Aaliyah-02.jpg/120px-Aaliyah-02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aaliyah-02.jpg)
Drake has credited [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West") (left) and [Aaliyah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaliyah "Aaliyah") (right) as being his biggest musical influences.
Drake is considered to be a [pop rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rap "Pop rap") artist.[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Suarez-257) While Drake's earlier music primarily spanned hip-hop and R&B, his music has delved into [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") and [trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_music "Trap music") since the albums _Nothing Was the Same_ (2013) and _Views_ (2016).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:5-19) Additionally, his music has drawn influence from regional scenes, including Jamaican dancehall[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:1-256) and [UK drill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_drill "UK drill").[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:0-190) Drake is known for his [egotistical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egotistical "Egotistical") lyrics, technical ability, and integration of personal backstory when dealing with relationships with women.[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-258) His vocal abilities have been lauded for an audible contrast between typical [hip-hop beats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop_production "Hip-hop production") and melody, with sometimes abrasive rapping coupled with softer accents, delivered on technical lyricism.[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Peak_Drake-259)
His songs often include audible changes in lyrical pronunciation in parallel with his upbringing in Toronto, and connections with [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean") and [Middle Eastern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_East "Middle East") countries which include such phrases as "ting", "touching road", "talkin' boasy" and "gwanin' wassy".[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Peak_Drake-259) Most of his songs contain R&B and [Canadian hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_hip-hop "Canadian hip-hop") elements, and he combines rapping with singing.[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Crowns_Himself-260) He credits his father with the introduction of singing into his rap mixtapes, which have become a staple in his musical repertoire. His incorporation of melody into technically complex lyrics was supported by Lil Wayne, and has subsequently been a critical component to Drake's singles and albums.[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-261) Drake's style of R&B is characterized by vacant beats and a [rap-sung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap-singing "Rap-singing") dichotomy, which has also seen incredible mainstream success, spawning several imitators.[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Charity-262)
The lyrical content that Drake deploys is typically considered to be emotional[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-263) or boastful.[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-264) However, Drake is often revered for incorporating "degrading" themes of money, drug use, and [women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misogyny_in_rap_music "Misogyny in rap music") into newer, idealized contexts, often achieving this through his augmentation of the typical meaning of phrases in which he combines an objective and subjective perspective into one vocal delivery. His songs often maintain tension between "pause and [pace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_acoustics "Musical acoustics"), [tone timbre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tone_cluster "Tone cluster"), and [volume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volume "Volume") and [vocal fermata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fermata "Fermata")".[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-265) Drake is credited with innovating what has been referred to as "hyper-reality rap", characterized by its focus on themes of celebrity as distinct from the "real world".[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-266)
## Public image
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/Drake_Madame_Tussauds_London_Wax_Figure.jpg/250px-Drake_Madame_Tussauds_London_Wax_Figure.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Drake_Madame_Tussauds_London_Wax_Figure.jpg)A wax figure of Drake in [Madame Tussauds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madame_Tussauds "Madame Tussauds")
Drake's lyrical subject matter, which often revolves around relationships, have had widespread use on social media through photo captions to reference emotions or personal situations.[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-267) However, this content has incited mixed reception from fans and critics, with some deeming him as sensitive and inauthentic, traits perceived as antithetical to traditional hip-hop culture.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-268)[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-269) He is also known for his large and extravagant lifestyle, including for high-end themed birthday parties; he maintained this image in his early career by renting a [Rolls-Royce Phantom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolls-Royce_Phantom_\(seventh_generation\) "Rolls-Royce Phantom \(seventh generation\)"), which he was eventually gifted in 2021.[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-270) He cultivated a reputation as a successful [gambler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gambler "Gambler"); between December 2021 and February 2022, he was reported to have made bets of over $1 billion, which included winnings ranging between $354,000 and $7 million,[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-271) however some of the forms of gambling he promotes, such as [roulette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roulette "Roulette"), have negative [expected values](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expected_value "Expected value").[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-272)
_[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")_ editor Maura Judkis credits Drake for popularizing the phrase "[YOLO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YOLO_\(motto\) "YOLO \(motto\)")" in the United States with his single "[The Motto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Motto_\(Drake_song\) "The Motto \(Drake song\)")", which stands for, "You only live once".[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-YOLO-95) Drake later popularized the term "The Six" in 2015 in relation to his hometown [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto"), subsequently becoming a point of reference to the city.[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-273) June 10 was declared "Drake Day" in [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston").[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-274)[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-275)[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-276) In 2016, Drake visited [Drake University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_University "Drake University") after a show in [Des Moines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Des_Moines "Des Moines") in response to an extensive social media campaign by students that began in 2009, advocating for his appearance.[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-277)[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-278) According to a report from [Confused.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confused.com "Confused.com"), Drake's Toronto home was one of the most [Googled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Googled "Googled") homes in the world, recording over a million annual searches in 2021; its features, such as its [NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA "NBA")-size indoor basketball court and [Kohler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kohler_Co. "Kohler Co.") Numi [toilet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toilet "Toilet"), have also received widespread media attention.[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-279)
The music video for "[Hotline Bling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotline_Bling "Hotline Bling")" went [viral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viral_phenomenon "Viral phenomenon") due to Drake's eccentric dance moves.[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-280) The video has been remixed, [memed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_meme "Internet meme"), and was heavily commented on due to the unconventional nature on the song,[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-galil-281) causing it to gain popularity on YouTube, and spawning several parodies.[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-greene-282) Drake has also been critiqued for his expensive, product placement-heavy attire, exemplified by the video for "Hotline Bling". Drake modelled a $1,500 [Moncler Puffer Jacket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moncler "Moncler"), a $400 [Acne Studios turtleneck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acne_Studios "Acne Studios"), and limited edition [Timberland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Timberland_Company "The Timberland Company") 6" Classic Boots.[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-283)[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-284) He was labelled by _[GQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GQ "GQ")_ magazine as "[one of] the most stylish men alive";[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-285) during promotion for _[Certified Lover Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Lover_Boy "Certified Lover Boy")_ , Drake debuted a "heart haircut", which became popular and widely imitated.[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-286) Writing for _GQ_ , Anish Patel noted Drake's consistent incorporation of styles and themes not typically associated with hip-hop, such as wearing [gorpcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gorpcore "Gorpcore") in the music video for his song "Sticky".[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-287) Since 2016 Drake has been noted for an alleged "Drake curse", an internet [meme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meme "Meme") based on the incidents where he appears to be support of particular sports team or person, just for that team or person to lose, often against the odds.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-288)[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-289)

the safety of [ethnic minorities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_and_ethnicity_in_the_United_States "Race and ethnicity in the United States") against police brutality in the United States.[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-290) In 2021, he joined a group of Canadian musicians to work with the [Songwriters Association of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriters_Association_of_Canada "Songwriters Association of Canada") (SAC) to lobby Prime Minister [Justin Trudeau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Trudeau "Justin Trudeau") to restructure the country's [copyright law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyright_law "Copyright law") to allow artists and their families to regain ownership of copyrights during their lifetime.[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-291) He also campaigned for the expansion of a [Women's National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_National_Basketball_Association "Women's National Basketball Association") (WNBA) [franchise in Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Tempo "Toronto Tempo"),[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-292) and headlined a [benefit concert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benefit_concert "Benefit concert") at the [Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Memorial_Coliseum "Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum") with Kanye West on December 9, 2021, to raise clemency for [Larry Hoover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Hoover "Larry Hoover"),[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-293) although his solo performance was later removed from the [Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Video "Prime Video") replay.[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-294) On October 20, 2023, Drake expressed solidarity with the people of Palestine amid the [Gaza War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_War "Gaza War"). He joined a coalition of actors, filmmakers, and artists in signing the [Artists4Ceasefire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artists4Ceasefire "Artists4Ceasefire") open letter, which called for an immediate and permanent ceasefire.[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-295) The letter stated: "We believe all life is sacred, no matter faith or ethnicity, and we condemn the killing of Palestinian and Israeli civilians."[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-296)
[Drake's 2024 feud with Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake%E2%80%93Kendrick_Lamar_feud "Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud") has been reported to have damaged his public image,[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-297) with _[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Yorker "The New Yorker")_ writing that audiences "delighted in abandoning Drake to side with Lamar" to the point that opposition to Drake "felt like a righteous political movement".[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-298) Lamar—who accused Drake of [pedophilia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedophilia "Pedophilia") in his number-one single "[Not Like Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us "Not Like Us")"—was widely considered to have won the feud,[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-299)[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-TheRinger:_Nail-300) and Drake was seen as a sore loser following his legal actions against Universal Music Group.[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-301) Justin Sayles of _[The Ringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ringer_\(website\) "The Ringer \(website\)")_ wrote the feud "[saw] Drake sink to the lowest levels of his career",[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-TheRinger:_Nail-300) and Gene Park of _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")_ and the music journalist Peter A. Berry described his loss as an unparalleled humiliation.[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-302)[[300]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-AP:_Comeback-303) [Sowmya Krishnamurthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sowmya_Krishnamurthy "Sowmya Krishnamurthy") said the feud ended the popular perception of Drake as the leading hip-hop figure.[[300]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-AP:_Comeback-303)
In September 2026, following the [Fear of Missing Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear_of_Missing_Out "Fear of Missing Out") premiere, listeners noted that a song snippet appearing roughly 17 minutes into the film, Drake said "pray for Gaza."[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-complex-gaza-304) [Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_\(magazine\) "Complex \(magazine\)")'s Shawn Setaro wrote that the line's meaning was ambiguous, noting it could reference the [Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip "Gaza Strip") or, given the song's dancehall influence, serve as a reference to Jamaican dancehall artist [Vybz Kartel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vybz_Kartel "Vybz Kartel"), who refers to his home region of [Portmore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portmore,_Jamaica "Portmore, Jamaica") as "Gaza City" and to his fanbase as "Gaza nation," or potentially both.[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-complex-gaza-304)
## Impact
A prominent figure in [pop culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_culture "Pop culture"),[[302]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-305) Drake is often praised one of the most influential figures in hip-hop;[[303]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:3-306) particularly his use of [rap-singing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap-singing "Rap-singing") has been noted as an influence on modern rappers.[[304]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-307) He is widely credited for popularizing the [Toronto sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_sound_\(hip-hop\) "Toronto sound \(hip-hop\)") to the music industry and leading the "Canadian Invasion", a play on the [British Invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Invasion "British Invasion") in the 1960s, of the American charts—alongside the likes of [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber") and [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd").[[305]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-308)[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-309)[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:8-310)[[308]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-311)[[309]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-312) In 2022, music recognition app [Shazam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shazam_\(music_app\) "Shazam \(music app\)") revealed Drake to be their most searched artist by users, with music featuring Drake collecting 350 million recognitions; his 2016 single "One Dance" collected 17 million recognitions alone.[[310]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-313) In 2018, articles by _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_ and _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ called him "the definitive pop star of his generation" and "perhaps [the] biggest post-[Justin Timberlake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Timberlake "Justin Timberlake") male pop star of the new millennium", respectively.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:5-19)[[311]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-rs_genre-314) In 2018, he was reportedly responsible for 5% (CAD$440 million) of Toronto's CAD$8.8 billion annual tourism income.[[312]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-315)
[_The Insider_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Insider_\(newsletter\) "The Insider \(newsletter\)") declared Drake the artist of the decade (2010s). Regarding the general view that Drake introduced singing in mainstream hip-hop, the publication said that at the height of [Auto-Tune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auto-Tune "Auto-Tune") in hip-hop during the late 2000s, "there were virtually no artists who were both a legit rapper and a legit crooner who delivered velvety smooth pop/R&B hybrid vocals that could exist separately from his hip-hop songs".[[303]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:3-306) Commenting on Drake's _Take Care_ , Elias Leight of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ noticed in 2020 that "now nearly every singer raps, and nearly every rapper sings", as many artists "have borrowed or copied the template of [the album] that the boldness of the original is easily forgotten", according to the writer.[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-rs500-316)
Aaron Williams of [Uproxx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uproxx "Uproxx") added "jump-starting the sad boy rapper craze alongside [Kid Cudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kid_Cudi "Kid Cudi")" and "helping to renew stateside interest in UK [grime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grime_\(music_genre\) "Grime \(music genre\)") and Caribbean [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall") with [Skepta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skepta "Skepta"), PartyNextDoor, and Rihanna" to the modern trends Drake assisted.[[314]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-317) [BBC Radio 1Xtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_1Xtra "BBC Radio 1Xtra") argued that his co-signs helped push the [British hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_hip-hop "British hip-hop") scene to a wider international market, as he did with the Toronto music scene.[[315]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-318) According to [CBS Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") in 2019, Drake has inspired "the next wave" of artists coming out of his hometown.[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:8-310) Writing for _[Bloomberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_L.P. "Bloomberg L.P.")_ , Lucas Shaw commented Drake's popularity has influenced the promotion of music, with _Certified Lover Boy_ attaining large commercial success despite relatively minimal orthodox marketing techniques, stating "fans are consuming Drake's [music] in a way that is different to others". He also noted the album as novel in relation to consumption, with each song having relatively equivalent [streams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media"), as opposed to a dominant [single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_\(music\) "Single \(music\)")(s).[[316]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Shaw-319) Justin Charity of [The Ringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ringer_\(website\) "The Ringer \(website\)") noted Drake's signature of producing "half-hearted" performances on songs to create a "natural and off-the-cuff" effect has become the "obvious touchpoint for [subsequent] male R&B singers". Charity further wrote Drake's success in the genre is "so thorough that it's all but impossible to hear certain vintages of R&B without hearing Drake".[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Charity-262)
Beginning in 2022, Drake's music was canonized academically by [Toronto Metropolitan University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Metropolitan_University "Toronto Metropolitan University"), which began teaching courses titled "Deconstructing Drake and the Weeknd", with the pair's music used to explore themes related to the Canadian music industry, race, class, marketing and globalization.[[317]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-320) With the release during [LGBT Pride Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_pride#LGBT_Pride_Month "LGBT pride") of his seventh album _[Honestly, Nevermind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honestly,_Nevermind "Honestly, Nevermind")_ (2022), Mark Savage of the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") wrote Drake's exploration of [house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music "House music"), a genre with overt origins in black and queer spaces, would help "build a bridge to those [origin] subcultures" for younger music listeners.[[318]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-321)
## Achievements
Main article: [List of awards and nominations received by Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Drake "List of awards and nominations received by Drake")
Drake is the [highest-certified digital singles artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-certified_music_artists_in_the_United_States "List of highest-certified music artists in the United States") ever in the United States, having moved 142 million units based on combined sales and on-demand streams.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-billboard_riaa2-11)[[319]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-322) His highest-certified single is "God's Plan" (15× Platinum), followed by "Hotline Bling" and "One Dance", which are certified Diamond.[[320]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-323) Drake was [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify")'s most streamed artist of the 2010s.[[321]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-324)
He holds several _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart records; he has the most charted songs of any artist (407), the most top 10 hits (91), the most top 10 debuts (75), the most top 10 singles in a calendar year (13), the most cumulative weeks in the top 10 (424), the most songs peaking at number-two (13) (14 including his appearance as a member of [Young Money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Money "Young Money") on "[BedRock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BedRock "BedRock")"),[[322]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-billboard-325)[[323]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-billboard.com-326) the most weeks spent at number one in a calendar year (29 weeks),[[324]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-327) and the most consecutive weeks spent on the chart (431 weeks).[[322]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-billboard-325)[[323]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-billboard.com-326) He has accumulated 14 number-one songs (15 including his feature on "[Sicko Mode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sicko_Mode "Sicko Mode")"), a record for a male solo artist.[[325]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-328)[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Sicko_mode-12) In 2021, Drake became the second act after [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles") in 1964 to simultaneously occupy the entire Hot 100's top five and the first to simultaneously chart nine songs in the top ten. He also has the most number-one singles on the [Hot Rap Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Rap_Songs "Hot Rap Songs") (33), [Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_R&B/Hip-Hop_Songs "Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs") (33),[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-billboard_drake-209) and [R&B/Hip-Hop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R&B/Hip-Hop_Airplay "R&B/Hip-Hop Airplay") (29).[[326]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-329) He is also the only artist to have two albums log 400 weeks each on the _Billboard_ 200.[[327]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-330)
As of 2026, Drake has won 5 [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") from 51 nominations.[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-331) He has also won a [record 29 _Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Award#Most_wins "Billboard Music Award"). In [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Billboard_Music_Awards "2017 Billboard Music Awards"), he surpassed [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele")'s record for most wins at the [Billboard Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Awards "Billboard Music Awards") in one night, winning 13 awards from 22 nominations.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-chicagotribune-157) He was named [Artist of the Decade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Artist_of_the_Decade_Award "Billboard Artist of the Decade Award") at the [2021 _Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Billboard_Music_Awards "2021 Billboard Music Awards").[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:2-206) _Billboard_ editor Ernest Baker stated "Drake managed to rule hip-hop in 2014", adding "the best rapper in 2014 didn't need a new album or hit single to prove his dominance".[[329]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-332) From 2015 to 2017, Drake ranked within the top-five of the _Billboard_ Year-End chart for Top Artists,[[330]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-333)[[331]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-334)[[332]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-335) before topping it in 2018.[[333]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-336) He was named the [IFPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFPI "IFPI") [Global Recording Artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Recording_Artist_of_the_Year "Global Recording Artist of the Year") of 2016 and 2018.[[334]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-337)
_Pitchfork_ ranked _Nothing Was the Same_ as the 41st best album of the decade "so far"—between 2010 and 2014,[[335]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-338) and ranked him fifth in the publication's list of the "Top 10 Music Artists" since 2010.[[336]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-339)[[337]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-340) _Take Care_ was ranked at number 95 on [_Rolling Stone_ 's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone's_500_Greatest_Albums_of_All_Time "Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time") (2020).[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-rs500-316) He has been ranked by _[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_\(magazine\) "Complex \(magazine\)")_ on their "Best Rapper Alive Every Year Since 1979" list, awarding Drake the accolade in 2011, 2012, and 2015.[[338]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-341)
## Legal issues
Further information: [List of Drake samples and sampling disputes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Drake_samples_and_sampling_disputes "List of Drake samples and sampling disputes")
In 2012, singer Ericka Lee filed a lawsuit against Drake for the usage of her voice on "[Marvins Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvins_Room "Marvins Room")". Claiming to have provided the female vocals, Lee also alleged she was owed songwriting credits and royalties.[[339]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-rollingstone-342) Despite Drake's legal team countering by claiming that Lee simply requested a credit in the liner notes of [the album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take_Care_\(album\) "Take Care \(album\)"), the matter was resolved in February 2013, with both parties agreeing to an [out-of-court settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Out-of-court_settlement "Out-of-court settlement").[[340]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-343) Also in 2012, Drake caused a nightclub in [Oklahoma City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City "Oklahoma City") to close down, due to his usage of [marijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marijuana "Marijuana") and other illegal drugs being prevalent at the club.[[341]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-344) In 2014, Drake was sued for $300,000 for sampling "Jimmy Smith Rap", a 1982 single by jazz musician [Jimmy Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Smith_\(musician\) "Jimmy Smith \(musician\)"). The suit was filed by Smith's estate, who said Drake [never asked for permission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_use "Fair use") when sampling it for the intro on "[Pound Cake / Paris Morton Music 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pound_Cake_/_Paris_Morton_Music_2 "Pound Cake / Paris Morton Music 2")", claiming Smith himself would have disagreed as he disliked hip-hop.[[342]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-345)[[343]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-346) Drake would win the lawsuit in 2017, with federal judge [William Pauley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Pauley "William Pauley") ruling the content used was transformative, and there was no liability for copyright infringement.[[344]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-347) Also in 2014, it emerged that Drake was sued by rapper [Rappin' 4-Tay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rappin'_4-Tay "Rappin' 4-Tay"), claiming Drake misused his lyrics when collaborating with [YG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YG_\(rapper\) "YG \(rapper\)") on the song "[Who Do You Love?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who_Do_You_Love%3F_\(YG_song\) "Who Do You Love? \(YG song\)")". He sought $100,000 for mistreatment and artistic theft, which Drake paid to the rapper later that year.[[345]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-pitchfork.com2-348)
In December 2021, Drake sued jeweller Ori Vechler and his company Gemma LTD for incorrectly using his likeness in promotional material; he also sought to return three items he purchased.[[346]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-349) In December 2022, a lawsuit brought by rapper Angelou Skywalker, who alleged that Drake stole his song "Reach for Skies" to make "[Way 2 Sexy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Way_2_Sexy "Way 2 Sexy")", was dismissed following "repeated misconduct" by Skywalker against prosecutors and US district judge Colleen Kollar-Kotelly, who presided over the case; Skywalker was accused of filing no less than 50 irrelevant motions and was handed a restraining order, preventing contact with Drake.[[347]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-350)
In 2017, Drake was embroiled in another lawsuit, being sued by producer [Detail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detail_\(record_producer\) "Detail \(record producer\)") (Noel Fisher) over an alleged assault in 2014. Fisher claimed Drake's bodyguard, Nessel "Chubbs" Beezer, punched him in the face and allegedly broke his jaw over musical and financial disputes. Fisher also said the injuries caused him to be hospitalized for days and had to undergo several surgeries, following which he sued for damages related to medical bills and physical and emotional suffering.[[348]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-351) The case, which was set to undergo trial in May 2018, was dismissed by Superior Court Judge Elaine Lu after Fisher failed to show up for a final status conference. Lu ruled that Beezer solely acted in self-defense.[[349]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-352)
In January 2019, Drake, [Odell Beckham Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odell_Beckham_Jr. "Odell Beckham Jr."), and Younes Bendjima were sued by a man named Bennett Sipes in regards to an alleged assault that occurred outside of a L.A. nightclub in 2018. Sipes claims he suffered "traumatic brain injury, as well as injuries to his back, neck, shoulders, etc." on March 24, 2018, when he was attacked by Bendjima, as well as members of Drake and Beckham's entourages in an alley near the nightclub and sought $250,000 in damages. The suit alleges Drake and Beckham followed their respective crews to the alley to watch Sipes get attacked. A video of the incident was recorded using the on-site surveillance system.[[350]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-353) The suit was eventually settled out of court.[[351]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-354) In 2019, Drake paid a $350,000 settlement to a woman who alleged that he sexually assaulted her. Drake denied the allegations.[[352]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-355)
In October 2021, Drake and [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown "Chris Brown") were sued by Braindon Cooper and Timothy Valentine for [copyright infringement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyright_infringement "Copyright infringement") between "[No Guidance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Guidance "No Guidance")" and their own song "I Love Your Dress",[[353]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-356)[[354]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-357)[[355]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-358) but Drake was dropped by Cooper and Valentine from the lawsuit in April 2022.[[356]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-359) Drake was handed another copyright lawsuit from Samuel Nicholas, citing infringement from Drake's "[In My Feelings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_My_Feelings "In My Feelings")" and "[Nice for What](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nice_for_What "Nice for What")".[[357]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-360) That November, he was named co-defendant with [Travis Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travis_Scott "Travis Scott") in a multi-claimant lawsuit for inciting "[a riot and violence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astroworld_Festival_crowd_crush "Astroworld Festival crowd crush")" at the [Astroworld Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astroworld_Festival "Astroworld Festival"),[[358]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-361) to which he released a statement;[[359]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-362) he reportedly delayed the release of "Splash Brothers", a collaboration with [French Montana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Montana "French Montana"), as a result.[[360]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-363)
On July 14, 2022, Drake was detained by [Swedish police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_police "Swedish police"), reportedly stemming from drugs present within a [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm") nightclub.[[361]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-364) That November, Drake and [21 Savage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21_Savage "21 Savage") were sued by [Condé Nast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cond%C3%A9_Nast "Condé Nast"), the publisher of _[Vogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vogue_\(magazine\) "Vogue \(magazine\)")_ , for using the _Vogue_ name without permission to promote their collaborative album _[Her Loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_Loss "Her Loss")_ ;[[362]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-365)[[363]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-366) Drake and 21 Savage "voluntarily ceased" to a preliminary injunction to stop using _Vogue_ trademarks to promote the album,[[364]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-367) and later reached a settlement with Condé Nast.[[365]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-368) In February 2023, Drake was ordered to appear for a [deposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deposition_\(law\) "Deposition \(law\)") in the [XXXTentacion murder trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XXXTentacion_murder_trial "XXXTentacion murder trial") after the defence team for Dedrick Williams—one of the three suspects—listed Drake as a potential witness, related to the purported feud between Drake and XXXTentacion; Drake was subpoenaed the month prior, and failed to show for his scheduled deposition date of January 27; the rescheduled deposition was set for February 24.[[366]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-369) It was later reported that armed guards at Drake's Beverly Hills home refused to accept the service of the deposition on February 14, which Drake's lawyer, [Bradford Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradford_Cohen "Bradford Cohen"), argued was not properly served in compliance with California law and done solely to "inject celebrity spectacle in a routine trial", ultimately leading to the deposition being dismissed.[[367]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-370)
In November 2024, Drake initiated a legal petition against [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group") (UMG), the parent company of [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records"), with whom Drake has a [recording contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_contract "Recording contract"), and [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), alleging they conspired to artificially inflate the number of streams of the [diss track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diss_track "Diss track") "[Not Like Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us "Not Like Us")" during [Drake's feud with Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake's_feud_with_Kendrick_Lamar "Drake's feud with Kendrick Lamar") earlier that year by implementing [pay-to-play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payola "Payola") schemes, [malicious bots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_bot#Malicious_bots "Internet bot"), and other tactics.[[368]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-371) Drake withdrew the petition on January 14, 2025, and filed a lawsuit in the US [District Court for the Southern District of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_Court_for_the_Southern_District_of_New_York "District Court for the Southern District of New York") a day later, alleging [defamation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defamation "Defamation") against UMG for promoting "Not Like Us".[[369]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-372)[[370]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-373) In February, UMG filed to pause [discovery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_\(law\) "Discovery \(law\)") until their motion to dismiss the case is heard on June 30. On April 3, judge [Jeannette Vargas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeannette_Vargas "Jeannette Vargas") ordered for discovery to continue, resulting in access to contracts between UMG and Lamar, as well as salaries and incentive plans for senior record label staff going back to 2020, being handed over to Drake.[[371]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-374) On April 18, Drake expanded the lawsuit against UMG by also alleging defamation by Lamar's [halftime performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX_halftime_show "Super Bowl LIX halftime show") of "Not Like Us" at [Super Bowl LIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX "Super Bowl LIX").[[372]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-375) The suit was dismissed in October 2025, with the court finding the allegedly defamatory statements to be nonactionable opinion.[[373]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-376)
A lawsuit against Drake, internet personality [Adin Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adin_Ross "Adin Ross"), and online casino [Stake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stake_\(online_casino\) "Stake \(online casino\)") was filed in federal court in Missouri on October 27, 2025. The filing alleges that Drake and Ross illegally misled viewers during gambling livestreams by presenting Stake-funded bets as personal wagers.[[374]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-377) A second lawsuit was filed against Drake, Ross, and Stake's parent company Sweepstakes in New Mexico on October 30, making the same allegations.[[375]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-378) Another lawsuit against Drake, Ross, Stake, Sweepstakes, and Australian national George Nguyen, alleging that Drake funnelled Stake money to Nguyen in exchange for artificially boosted numbers on music streaming services, was filed in federal court in Virginia on December 31, 2025.[[376]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-379)
## Feuds and public disputes
See also: [Drake–Kanye West feud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake%E2%80%93Kanye_West_feud "Drake–Kanye West feud") and [Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake%E2%80%93Kendrick_Lamar_feud "Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud")
Drake and [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown "Chris Brown") were allegedly involved in a physical altercation in June 2012 when Drake and his entourage threw glass bottles at Brown in a [SoHo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoHo "SoHo") nightclub in [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), New York City. Chris Brown tweeted about the incident, and criticized Drake in music until 2013, including on the "[R.I.P.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R.I.P._\(Young_Jeezy_song\)#Remixes "R.I.P. \(Young Jeezy song\)")" remix.[[377]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-380)[[378]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-381)[[379]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-382) In 2014, he and Brown both appeared in a comedic skit for the [ESPY](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPY "ESPY") Awards, and rehearsed the skit together prior to the televised airing, virtually ending the dispute.[[380]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-383) The pair later collaborated on the Diamond certified "[No Guidance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Guidance "No Guidance")" in 2019.[[381]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-384)
The Drake-[Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") feud was identified by media outlets from 2013, alleging several songs to be [sneak disses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sneak_diss "Sneak diss") by both parties. Lamar first [dissed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diss_\(music\) "Diss \(music\)") Drake and other rappers on the song "[Control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Control_\(Big_Sean_song\) "Control \(Big Sean song\)")" in 2013, but stated his verse was intended to be seen as "friendly competition": Drake and Lamar previously collaborated on songs and Lamar featured as Drake's opening act on the [Club Paradise Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Paradise_Tour "Club Paradise Tour") in 2012. Lamar dissed Drake and [J. Cole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Cole "J. Cole") in 2024, with Drake and J. Cole's 2023 song "[First Person Shooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Person_Shooter_\(song\) "First Person Shooter \(song\)")" alleged to be a sneak diss. Drake responded on the songs "[Push Ups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push_Ups_\(song\) "Push Ups \(song\)")" and "[Taylor Made Freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Made_Freestyle "Taylor Made Freestyle")", of which, Lamar responded with "[Euphoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphoria_\(Kendrick_Lamar_song\) "Euphoria \(Kendrick Lamar song\)")" and "[6:16 in LA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6:16_in_LA "6:16 in LA")". Drake then released "[Family Matters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Matters_\(Drake_song\) "Family Matters \(Drake song\)")", accusing Lamar of domestic abuse and alleging one of Lamar's children was fathered by [Dave Free](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Free "Dave Free"). Lamar first replied with "[Meet the Grahams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meet_the_Grahams "Meet the Grahams")", accusing Drake of sex crimes and fathering a secret child, and then with "[Not Like Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Like_Us "Not Like Us")", accusing Drake of [pedophilia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedophilia "Pedophilia") and anti-black sentiment.[[382]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-385) Drake responded with "[The Heart Part 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Heart_Part_6 "The Heart Part 6")", denying Lamar's accusations and claiming he gave Lamar false information about the secret child.[[383]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-:7-386)
In December 2014, Drake was involved in another altercation, being punched by [Sean Combs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Combs "Sean Combs") outside the nightclub [LIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LIV_\(nightclub\) "LIV \(nightclub\)") in [Miami Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Beach "Miami Beach"). The altercation was reported to be over Drake's usage of the instrumental for "[0 to 100 / The Catch Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/0_to_100_/_The_Catch_Up "0 to 100 / The Catch Up")", allegedly produced by [Boi-1da](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boi-1da "Boi-1da") for Combs, before Drake appropriated it for himself. Drake was rushed to the ER after aggravating an old arm injury during the dispute.[[384]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-387) Drake was also involved in a feud with [Tyga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyga "Tyga"), stemming from Tyga's negative comments about him during an interview with _[Vibe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibe_\(magazine\) "Vibe \(magazine\)")_ magazine.[[385]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-388) Drake would later respond on "6 God" and "6PM in New York", which has been interpreted as directly involved in Tyga's abrupt removal from [Young Money Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Money_Entertainment "Young Money Entertainment").[[386]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-389)
Controversy arose in July 2015 when [Meek Mill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meek_Mill "Meek Mill") alleged that Drake had used [ghostwriters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghostwriter "Ghostwriter") for his verse on "[R.I.C.O.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R.I.C.O. "R.I.C.O.")". This was followed by further allegations that Drake did not help promote the song because Meek Mill discovered the ghostwriter, whom he revealed to be [Quentin Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quentin_Miller "Quentin Miller").[[387]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-BallerStatus.com2-390) Despite Miller [receiving past writing credits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_You're_Reading_This_It's_Too_Late#Track_listing "If You're Reading This It's Too Late"), [Funkmaster Flex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funkmaster_Flex "Funkmaster Flex") aired [reference tracks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demo_\(music\) "Demo \(music\)") by Miller, who was revealed to have helped write "R.I.C.O.", "10 Bands", and "Know Yourself". This prompted Drake to respond with two [diss tracks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diss_track "Diss track"): "[Charged Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charged_Up "Charged Up")" and "[Back to Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_to_Back_\(Drake_song\) "Back to Back \(Drake song\)")",[[388]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-391)[[389]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-392) in the space of four days. Meek Mill responded with "[Wanna Know](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanna_Know_\(Meek_Mill_song\) "Wanna Know \(Meek Mill song\)")",[[390]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-393) before removing it from [SoundCloud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoundCloud "SoundCloud") weeks later.[[391]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-ew.com2-394) Following several subliminal disses[[392]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-mtv.com2-395)[[393]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Bossip2-396)[[394]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-397) from either artist,[[395]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-398) Drake further sought to denounce Funkmaster Flex while performing in New York (Flex's home state) on the [Summer Sixteen Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Sixteen_Tour "Summer Sixteen Tour").[[396]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-399)[[397]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-400) After Meek Mill's 2017 prison sentence for probation violation, Drake stated "Free Meek Mill" at a concert in Australia, and ended their rivalry on "Family Feud" in 2018;[[398]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-401) the pair later collaborated on "[Going Bad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Going_Bad "Going Bad")" in 2019.[[399]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-402)
[Pusha T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pusha_T "Pusha T") would use the same rationale to diss Drake on "Infrared" in 2018,[[400]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-403) leading Drake to respond with the "[Duppy Freestyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duppy_Freestyle "Duppy Freestyle")" diss track on May 25.[[401]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-404) Pusha T responded with "[The Story of Adidon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_of_Adidon "The Story of Adidon")" on May 29, which presented several claims and revealed [Drake's fatherhood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#Family_and_relationships).[[402]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-405) The pair are considered to have been in a rivalry since 2012, resulting from Pusha T's feuds with [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne") and [Birdman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birdman_\(rapper\) "Birdman \(rapper\)"), with Drake yet to respond to "The Story of Adidon".[[403]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-406)
In 2016, Drake was embroiled in a feud with [Joe Budden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Budden "Joe Budden"), stemming from Budden's derogatory comments when reviewing _Views_. Drake would allegedly respond to Budden through "4PM in Calabasas", prompting Budden to respond with two diss tracks in the space of five days, echoing the same sentiment Drake deployed during his feud with Meek Mill. Drake would later appear on "[No Shopping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Shopping "No Shopping")" alongside [French Montana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Montana "French Montana"), directly referencing Budden throughout the song, although, Montana claimed Drake's verse was recorded before the release of Budden's diss tracks. Despite Budden releasing two further songs in reference to Drake,[[404]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-407) he has yet to officially respond to Budden.[[405]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-408) In the same year, Drake dissed [Kid Cudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kid_Cudi "Kid Cudi") on "Two Birds, One Stone" after Cudi launched an expletive-filled rant on the artist on Twitter.[[406]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-409) Cudi later checked into a [rehabilitation facility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_rehabilitation "Drug rehabilitation") following the release of the song, and continued to disparage Drake in further tweets;[[407]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-410) the pair eventually resolved their feud, and collaborated on "IMY2" in 2021.[[408]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-411)
In mid-2018, Drake was embroiled in a feud with long-time collaborator [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West").[[409]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-412) In an appearance on _The Shop_ , Drake recounted several meetings with West, who voiced his desire to "be [Quincy Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy_Jones "Quincy Jones")" and work with Drake and replicate the producer-artist relationship between Jones and [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson").[[410]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-413) West requested Drake play and inform him of upcoming releases, while he gave Drake the instrumental to "[Lift Yourself](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lift_Yourself "Lift Yourself")".[[411]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-414) West requested the pair work in [Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming "Wyoming"), with Drake arriving a day after close friend [40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40_\(record_producer\) "40 \(record producer\)"), who said West was instead recording [an album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ye_\(album\) "Ye \(album\)"). Judging the pair to have differing release schedules, Drake travelled to Wyoming,[[412]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-415) but "only worked on [West's] music"; they explored Drake's after he played West "[March 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorpion_\(Drake_album\)#Track_listing "Scorpion \(Drake album\)")", which addressed Drake's relationship with his newborn son and co-parent.[[413]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-416) This prompted a conversation with West regarding his personal issues, after which, news of his son would be exposed by Pusha T,[[414]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-417) which Drake concluded was revealed to him by West; West also released "Lift Yourself" as a solo song and produced "Infrared". Drake then denounced West in songs and live performances.[[415]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-418)[[416]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-419) West would retaliate in a series of tweets in late 2018, and the pair continued to respond on social media and in music as of late 2021,[[417]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-420) which included Drake leaking West's song "Life of the Party".[[418]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-421) During their feud, West and Drake have had public attempts of reconciliation,[[419]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-422) which is reported to have occurred after they co-headlined a benefit concert in December 2021.[[420]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-423)
Drake has been involved in reported feuds with [DMX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DMX "DMX"), music critic [Anthony Fantano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Fantano "Anthony Fantano"),[[421]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Fantano_1,_Drake_0-424)[[422]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Fantano_2,_Drake_0-425)[[423]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Fantano_3,_Drake_0-426) [Common](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_\(rapper\) "Common \(rapper\)"),[[424]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-427) [the Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd"),[[425]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-428) [XXXTentacion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XXXTentacion "XXXTentacion"), [Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z"), [Tory Lanez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tory_Lanez "Tory Lanez"),[[426]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-429) and [Ludacris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludacris "Ludacris"),[[427]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-430) although the latter three, as well as his feud with DMX, have been reported to be resolved.[[428]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-431)[[429]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-432)[[430]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-433)
## Business ventures
### Endorsements
Prior to venturing into business, Drake garnered several endorsement deals with various companies, notably gaining one with [Sprite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprite_\(soft_drink\) "Sprite \(soft drink\)") following his mention of drinking [purple drank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purple_drank "Purple drank"), a concoction that contains Sprite as a key ingredient.[[431]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-434)[[432]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-435) Business magazine _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")_ commented his endorsement deals and business partnerships "combined heavily" for Drake's reported pre-tax earnings at $94 million between June 2016 to June 2017, being one of the highest-paid celebrities during that period.[[433]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-436) Drake receives an endorsement of $100 million per annum from the gambling firm [Stake.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stake.com "Stake.com"), as an ambassador of the online casino.[[434]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-437) The partnership with Stake.com has created "The Drake Effect", which has increased the company's awareness.[[435]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-438)[[436]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-439) In January 2022, Drake announced Stake's two-year naming sponsorship of the Sauber Formula 1 (F1) racing team, which began in 2024.[[437]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-440)
### OVO Sound
Main article: [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound")
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/OVO_Sound.png/250px-OVO_Sound.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:OVO_Sound.png)The logo of Drake's [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound") imprint
During the composition of _Nothing Was the Same_ , Drake started his own record label in late 2012 with producer [Noah "40" Shebib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_"40"_Shebib "Noah "40" Shebib") and business partner Oliver El-Khatib. Drake sought for an avenue to release his own music, as well helping in the nurturing of other artists, while Shebib and El-Khatib yearned to start a label with a distinct sound, prompting the trio to team up to form [OVO Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OVO_Sound "OVO Sound").[[438]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-441) The name is an abbreviation derived from the October's Very Own moniker Drake used to publish his earlier projects. The label is currently distributed by [Warner Bros. Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Records "Warner Bros. Records").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
Drake, 40, and [PartyNextDoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PartyNextDoor "PartyNextDoor") were the label's inaugural artists. The label houses artists including Drake, PartyNextDoor, [Majid Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majid_Jordan "Majid Jordan"), [Roy Woods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Woods "Roy Woods"), and [dvsn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dvsn "Dvsn"),[[439]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-442) as well as producers including 40, [Boi-1da](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boi-1da "Boi-1da"), [Nineteen85](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen85 "Nineteen85"), and Future the Prince.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
### Toronto Raptors
Main article: [Toronto Raptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Raptors "Toronto Raptors")
On September 30, 2013, at a press conference with [Maple Leaf Sports and Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maple_Leaf_Sports_and_Entertainment "Maple Leaf Sports and Entertainment") CEO [Tim Leiweke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Leiweke "Tim Leiweke"),[[440]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-betraptors2013-443) Drake was announced as the new "global ambassador" of the [Toronto Raptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Raptors "Toronto Raptors"), joining the executive committee of the [NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA "NBA") franchise. It was announced together with the [2016 NBA All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_All-Star_Game "2016 NBA All-Star Game") being awarded to the [Air Canada Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Canada_Centre "Air Canada Centre") in Toronto.[[441]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-444)[[442]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-445)[[443]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-446) This was also the setting where Drake was given [The Key to the City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Keys_to_the_City_in_Canada#Toronto "List of Keys to the City in Canada").[[444]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-447) In the role, it was announced that Drake would help to promote and serve as a host of festivities, beginning with the All-Star Game. He would also provide consulting services to rebrand the team, helping to redesign its image and clothing line in commemoration of the franchise's [20th anniversary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014-15_Toronto_Raptors_season "2014-15 Toronto Raptors season").[[440]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-betraptors2013-443)[[445]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-448)[[446]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-globeandmailraptors2013-449)[[447]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-450) He also collaborated with the Raptors on pre-game practice jerseys, t-shirts, and sweatsuits,[[448]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-451) and began hosting an annual "Drake Night" segment with the organization, beginning in 2013.[[449]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-452)
### Entertainment
#### Apple Music
Main article: [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music")
Following the [launch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_more_thing "One more thing") of [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music"), a music and video streaming service developed by [Apple Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. "Apple Inc."), the company announced Drake as the figurehead for the platform at their [Worldwide Developers Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worldwide_Developers_Conference "Worldwide Developers Conference") in 2015, with the artist also penning an exclusivity deal with the service worth a reported $19 million.[[450]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Announcement_by_Ars_Technica-453) This saw all future solo releases by Drake becoming available first on Apple Music, before seeing roll out to other streaming services and music retailers.[[451]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-454) Drake had also developed the OVO Sound Radio station on [Beats 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_1 "Beats 1"), which is utilized as the primary avenue for debuting singles and projects, with the station overseeing over 300 million unique users when it debuted _[More Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/More_Life "More Life")_.[[452]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-455) Drake's partnership with Apple Music has largely been credited for the platform's sharp success, as it attained 10 million subscribers after six months, as well as giving birth to exclusivity from artists, with many independent and signed artists, such as [Frank Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Ocean "Frank Ocean") and the Weeknd, also brokering exclusivity deals with streaming services.[[453]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-456) Through signing with the company, Drake was one of the artists, alongside [Pharrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharrell "Pharrell") and [Katy Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Perry "Katy Perry"), to exclusively own an [Apple Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Watch "Apple Watch") before the [smartwatch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smartwatch "Smartwatch") saw public release.[[454]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-457)
#### DreamCrew and investments
Main article: [DreamCrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DreamCrew "DreamCrew")
In 2017, Drake and Adel "Future" Nur co-founded the production company [DreamCrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DreamCrew "DreamCrew"), with functions in both management and entertainment. The company has produced the television series _[Euphoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euphoria_\(American_TV_series\) "Euphoria \(American TV series\)")_ and _[Top Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Boy "Top Boy")_.[[455]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-458) Their debut produced film was sports documentary _[The Carter Effect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Carter_Effect "The Carter Effect")_ , detailing the impact of [Vince Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Carter "Vince Carter") in [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada").[[456]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-459) On August 5, 2022, Drake was among those nominated for a [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Drama_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series") for acting as a producer on _Euphoria_.[[457]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-460)
In July 2021, Drake was announced as an executive producer, alongside [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James") and [Maverick Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maverick_Carter "Maverick Carter"), for _Black Ice_ , a documentary film charting the experiences of [black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_players_in_ice_hockey "Black players in ice hockey") and ethnic minority professional and amateur ice hockey players. It is due to be produced by Uninterrupted Canada in partnership with Drake's DreamCrew Entertainment, James' [SpringHill Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpringHill_Company "SpringHill Company"), and [Bell Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_Media "Bell Media").[[458]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-461) DreamCrew also began production on the unscripted survival series _Chillin' Island_ in 2021, due to air on [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO").[[459]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Blanchet-462) In June 2021, [Live Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Nation "Live Nation") confirmed a long-standing partnership with Drake to open History, a 2,500 convertible capacity live-entertainment and general function venue in Toronto. It was in development for over three years and is situated in [The Beaches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beaches,_Toronto "The Beaches, Toronto").[[460]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-463) He also aided in the venue's interior design, which contains LED screens, soundproofing, quick-change rooms and a customizable staircase.[[461]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-464) In November 2022, DreamCrew invested near-$100 million to revive the [open-air museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-air_museum "Open-air museum") and [amusement park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amusement_park "Amusement park") _[Luna Luna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luna_Luna_\(1987_exhibition\) "Luna Luna \(1987 exhibition\)")_ ; originally staged in [Hamburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburg "Hamburg"), it is set to go on a worldwide tour, with Drake stating, "[Luna Luna] is such a unique and special way to experience art. This is a big idea and opportunity that centers around what we love most: bringing people together".[[462]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-465)
Drake signed as an investor and collaborator with Los Angeles-based sustainability and financial services startup Aspiration; he will also use the company's enterprise services to monitor and ensure personal [carbon neutrality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_neutrality "Carbon neutrality").[[463]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-466) He has also invested in [robo-advisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robo-advisor "Robo-advisor") Wealthsimple, the "livestreaming video commerce platform" NTWRK, the cannabis provider Bullrider, and several sports-related ventures, including online esports betting platform Players' Lounge, the sportstech firm StatusPro, and online sports network Overtime. In an analysis by Brennan Doherty for _[Toronto Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Star "Toronto Star")_ , Drake's investment "carry all the hallmarks" typical of musicians, which is often [momentum investing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Momentum_investing "Momentum investing"), and cited Jason Pereira, who described Drake's business deals as typically [angel investing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel_investing "Angel investing") and [private equity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_equity "Private equity") (often [venture capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venture_capital "Venture capital")) funds. Pereira also noted his "leveraging his personal brand to generate cash".[[464]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Doherty-467) On August 30, 2022, it was reported that Drake and [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James"), as part of the investment fund Main Street Advisors, would partner with US private equity group RedBird Capital and [Yankee Global Enterprises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Global_Enterprises "Yankee Global Enterprises") to purchase Italian soccer club [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") for a rumoured $1.2 billion.[[465]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-468) As a minority shareholder in the club, he is one of a group of investors who hold a 0.07% stake.[[466]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-469) Drake has also invested in cryptocurrency and NFT payment solutions firm MoonPay.[[467]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Egkolfopoulou_2022_d344-470)

In 2018, Drake purchased an ownership stake in the gaming organization [100 Thieves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/100_Thieves "100 Thieves"), joining as a co-founder and co-owner. ### Cuisine
Main article: [Virginia Black Whiskey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Black_Whiskey "Virginia Black Whiskey")
Two months prior to the release of _Views_ , Drake announced the development of [Virginia Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Black_Whiskey "Virginia Black Whiskey"), a [bourbon whiskey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourbon_whiskey "Bourbon whiskey").[[470]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-473) This would be his second foray into selling foodstuffs, previously partnering with celebrity chef [Susur Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susur_Lee "Susur Lee") to open Fring's Restaurant and Antonio Park to open the sports bar Pick 6ix, both in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto") and eventually closed.[[471]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-474)[[472]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-475) Virginia Black was created and distributed by [Proximo Spirits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximo_Spirits "Proximo Spirits") and Brent Hocking,[[473]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-476) a spirits producer who founded [DeLeón Tequila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeLe%C3%B3n_Tequila "DeLeón Tequila") in 2008.[[474]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-477) The company described the partnership as "fruitful [as they] share a passion for style, music, and the pursuit of taste [on] a quest to redefine whiskey".[[475]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-478) In 2021, using ratings compiled from [Vivino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivino "Vivino") and complimentary website Distiller, Virginia Black was ranked the worst value celebrity liquor for quality and price.[[476]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-479)
The product was launched in June 2016, and contained two, three and four-year old Bourbon whiskies. The company sold over 4,000 bottles in the first week domestically.[[477]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-480) The brand was also promoted and marketed through Drake's music and various tours, such as being part of the "Virginia Black VIP Lounge" additional package available for purchase during the [Summer Sixteen Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Sixteen_Tour "Summer Sixteen Tour"). Virginia Black shipped a further 30,000 units when rollout was extended to select international markets in late 2016.[[478]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-481) The company later aired commercials with Drake's father, Dennis Graham, which featured the mock tagline of "The Realest Dude Ever" (in reference toward "[The Most Interesting Man in the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Most_Interesting_Man_in_the_World "The Most Interesting Man in the World")" tagline employed by [Dos Equis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dos_Equis "Dos Equis")) after extending the sale of the drink to Europe in 2017.[[479]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-auto1-482) In 2019, Drake began collaborating with Hocking on Mod Sélection, a luxury range of [champagne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champagne "Champagne"),[[480]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-483) and in May 2021, formed part of a $40 million series B investment funding round led by D1 Capital Partners in Daring Foods Inc., a vegan [meat analogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meat_analogue "Meat analogue") corporation.[[481]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-484) That September, he purchased a minority stake in Californian food chain Dave's Hot Chicken,[[482]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-485) and organized a promotion on October 24, 2022, to give away free chicken to Toronto residents on his 36th birthday.[[483]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-486)
