### Family and relationships
Drake's paternal uncles are musicians [Larry Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Graham "Larry Graham") and [Teenie Hodges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenie_Hodges "Teenie Hodges").[[518]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-macleans-521) Larry Graham was a member of [Sly and the Family Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sly_and_the_Family_Stone "Sly and the Family Stone"),[[519]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-522) while Hodges contributed to songs for [Al Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Green "Al Green"), including "[Love and Happiness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_and_Happiness "Love and Happiness")", "[Here I Am (Come and Take Me)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here_I_Am_\(Come_and_Take_Me\) "Here I Am \(Come and Take Me\)")", and "[Take Me to the River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take_Me_to_the_River "Take Me to the River")".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Post-42)[[520]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-523)
Drake briefly dated Catya "Cat" Washington (known for her appearance on _[Bad Girls Club: Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Girls_Club:_Miami "Bad Girls Club: Miami")_) after the pair met on the set of the "[Best I Ever Had](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_I_Ever_Had "Best I Ever Had")" music video in 2009.[[521]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-524) Drake mentions Washington in his 2011 song "[Shot for Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shot_for_Me "Shot for Me")", and his verse on [The Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_\(rapper\) "The Game \(rapper\)")'s "Good Girls Go Bad" (also 2011).[[522]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-525)[[523]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-526)[[524]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-527)
Drake was in an [on-again, off-again relationship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On-again,_off-again_relationship "On-again, off-again relationship") with [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna") from 2009 to 2016.[[525]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-528) He has mentioned the relationship in every one of his studio albums,[[526]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-529) and when presenting Rihanna with the [Michael Jackson Video Vanguard Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson_Video_Vanguard_Award "Michael Jackson Video Vanguard Award") in 2016, he said "she's a woman I've been in love with since I was 22 years old".[[527]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-530) On his relationship with her, he said on the talk show _[The Shop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shop "The Shop")_ :
> As life takes shape and teaches you your own lessons, I end up in this situation where I don't have the fairy tale [of] 'Drake started a family with Rihanna, [it's] so perfect'. It looks so good on paper [and] I wanted it too at one time.[[528]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-531)
Drake is a father to a son, who was born on October 11, 2017, to French painter and former model Sophie Brussaux.[[529]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-532)[[530]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-People_father-533) Brussaux's pregnancy was the subject of several rumours after featuring in a [TMZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TMZ "TMZ") article in early 2017.[[531]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-Cut_father-534) After the nature of the pair's relationship was discussed in [Pusha T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pusha_T "Pusha T")'s "[The Story of Adidon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_of_Adidon "The Story of Adidon")", Drake confirmed his fatherhood on the album _Scorpion_ in 2018.[[532]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-CoS_father-535)[[533]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\)#cite_note-536)

headings.heading: 2010–2012: Musical breakthrough with _Thank Me Later_ and _Take Care_
2013–2015: _Nothing Was the Same_ and _If You're Reading This It's Too Late_
2015–2017: _What a Time to Be Alive_ , _Views_ , and _More Life_
2018–2019: _Scary Hours_ , _Scorpion_ , and _Care Package_ ; return to television
2019–2021: _Dark Lane Demo Tapes_ , _Scary Hours 2_ , and _Certified Lover Boy_
2022–2024: _Honestly, Nevermind_ , _Her Loss_ , _For All the Dogs_ , Kendrick Lamar feud, and _100 Gigs_
2025–present: _Some Sexy Songs 4 U_ , _Iceman_ , _Maid of Honour_ , _Habibti_ and _Fear of Missing Out_
